title: The Saltmere Compass
setting: Saltmere Maritime Museum, a stormy Saturday night in November, during the annual winter gala
victimOrIncident: The museum's prize exhibit, an 18th-century brass-and-gold ship's compass, vanished from its locked display case in the Harbour Room between 9:00 and 9:40 pm, while the guests were at dinner in the main hall. The Harbour Room lights went out for a few minutes around 9:15. No glass was broken.

truth.motive: Owen owes £4,000 to a man called Slade, due Monday. Slade's private collector offered to wipe the debt in exchange for the compass.
truth.method: At 9:15 Owen switched off the Harbour Room circuit at the service-corridor panel, which killed the lights and the case alarm. He opened the case with the spare key HR-2 from the maintenance key board, wrapped the compass in a rag and hid it in his canvas tool bag. The key tag snapped off and fell. He switched the circuit back on at 9:22 and carried the bag past the kitchen to the basement.

timeline.event: Owen tells Delia he is going down to the basement to nurse the old boiler.
Imogen slips into the Harbour Room to photograph the compass for a replica commission.
Imogen hears footsteps and hurries out, dropping her lens cap on the bench.
Delia does her security round: compass present, case locked. She initials the round sheet.
Delia begins her speech in the main hall. Imogen is seated at the mayor's table.
Owen switches off the Harbour Room circuit at the service-corridor panel. Only the Harbour Room corridor goes dark; the main hall stays lit.
Owen opens the case with spare key HR-2 and takes the compass. The key tag snaps off and falls.
Owen switches the circuit back on.
The kitchen porter sees Owen hurrying from the Harbour Room corridor toward the basement stairs, clutching his tool bag.
Delia takes a donor to see the compass, finds the case empty and raises the alarm.

suspects.name: Delia Marsh
suspects.personality: Precise, proud and clipped. Protective of the collection and of her reputation. Answers in tidy, formal sentences and bristles when her integrity is questioned.

portrait.prompt: A woman in her late fifties with a sharp silver bob, tailored dark green dress, reading glasses on a chain, stern composed expression.

knows: At 8:30 Owen told me he was going down to the basement to nurse the old boiler.
I did my security round at 9:00. The compass was in its case and the case was locked. I initialled the round sheet.
I gave my speech in the main hall from 9:05 to about 9:30, with everyone watching.
The case has two keys: mine, which was on the chain at my wrist all night, and a spare tagged HR-2 that hangs on the maintenance key board.
When the Harbour Room lights went out around 9:15, the main hall stayed perfectly lit. I thought that was odd for a storm.
At 9:40 I took a donor to see the compass. The case was empty and unlocked, not forced. I raised the alarm.
Owen has been distracted for weeks, taking hushed phone calls out in the loading bay.
Imogen Vale offered to buy the compass last year and I refused her.
suspects.secret: The board voted in private to sell the compass to pay for the roof, and I arranged a confidential valuation with Hale and Crane Auctions for Monday. I'm ashamed of it and the board told me to keep it quiet.
suspects.lie: The compass would never be sold, not while I'm curator. I haven't spoken to any auction house, and I never would.

suspects.name: Owen Pryce
suspects.personality: Affable and folksy. Deflects with jokes and talk of the old building's quirks, but turns curt and short when pinned down on times and places.

portrait.prompt: A man in his forties with stubble and tousled dark hair, grey work shirt with rolled sleeves, a canvas tool belt, an easy grin that doesn't reach his tired eyes.

knows: I owe a man called Slade four thousand pounds, due Monday. His collector friend said he'd wipe the debt for the compass.
At 9:15 I flipped the Harbour Room circuit off at the panel in the service corridor. That kills the lights and the case alarm.
I opened the case with the spare key HR-2 from my key board, wrapped the compass in a rag and put it in my canvas tool bag.
The key tag snapped off the ring somewhere in the dark. I didn't stop to look for it.
I switched the circuit back on at about 9:22 and went down to the basement past the kitchen.
The compass is in my tool bag, tucked behind the boiler.
The Harbour Room lights and the case alarm both run off the panel in the service corridor.
The building's wiring is old, but the main supply never dropped tonight.
suspects.secret: I took the compass. I switched off the Harbour Room circuit, used the spare key and hid the compass in my tool bag behind the boiler to pay off my debt to Slade.
suspects.lie: I was down in the basement wrestling with the boiler from 8:30 until the alarm went up at 9:40, and I never set foot upstairs. The lights went out because of the storm, this old place does that. And nobody touches my key board, the keys never leave it.

suspects.name: Imogen Vale
suspects.personality: Languid, witty and faintly condescending. Treats the questioning as a parlour game and answers with dry asides, until she feels genuinely cornered.

portrait.prompt: A woman in her thirties with sleek black hair pinned up, pearl earrings, a deep plum velvet evening gown, an amused, slightly superior half-smile.

knows: I offered Delia sixty thousand pounds for the compass last year. She refused, rather rudely.
At 8:50 I slipped into the Harbour Room to photograph the compass for a replica I've commissioned. It was there and the case was locked.
I heard footsteps at about 8:56 and hurried out. I must have left my lens cap on the bench.
From 9:00 I was seated beside the mayor in the main hall until the alarm. He can vouch for me.
Around 9:15 I saw the lights in the Harbour Room corridor go dark through the doorway, but the main hall never so much as flickered.
During the speech I saw a man in a grey work shirt hurry past the kitchen doors toward the back stairs, hugging a bag.
suspects.secret: I sneaked into the Harbour Room before dinner to photograph the compass so a craftsman can make me a replica. Photography is forbidden and it would embarrass me terribly.
suspects.lie: I never left the dining table all evening. I haven't been anywhere near the Harbour Room tonight.

evidence.label: Opened display case
evidence.description: The compass case was opened with a key: the lock is undamaged and the little brass door stands ajar. The velvet cushion still holds the round imprint of the compass.
evidence.imagePrompt: An empty glass museum display case on a wooden pedestal, its small brass door ajar, a velvet cushion with the round imprint of a missing compass.

evidence.label: Brass key tag HR-2
evidence.description: A brass key tag stamped HR-2, lying on the floor by the pedestal. Its split ring has snapped. HR-2 is the spare for the compass case, kept on the maintenance key board.
evidence.imagePrompt: A small brass key tag with a snapped split ring lying on a parquet floor, stamped with a short code.

evidence.label: Engraved lens cap
evidence.description: A black camera lens cap on the bench beside the case, engraved with the initials I.V.
evidence.imagePrompt: A black camera lens cap with a small engraved monogram, resting on a polished wooden bench.

evidence.label: Telephone message slip
evidence.description: A message slip on the side table, in the receptionist's hand: "Mr. Hale of Hale & Crane Auctions phoned for Ms. Marsh. Valuation of the compass confirmed for Monday, 10 am."
evidence.imagePrompt: A folded paper message slip on a small antique side table beside a brass desk lamp.

evidence.label: Service-corridor panel log
evidence.description: The electrical panel's event log: Harbour Room circuit switched OFF manually at 9:15:40 pm and back ON manually at 9:21:55 pm. The main supply never dropped. No storm surge was recorded.

evidence.label: Kitchen porter's statement
evidence.description: "About 9:25, Owen came fast up the service corridor from the Harbour Room side, out of breath, holding his canvas tool bag tight against his chest. He went straight down the basement stairs."

evidence.label: Security round sheet
evidence.description: Delia's clipboard round sheet: "9:00 pm, Harbour Room: compass present, case locked. D.M."

between: Owen Pryce: "The lights went out because of the storm."
Panel log: the Harbour Room circuit was switched off and on by hand; the main supply never dropped.
keyContradictions.explanation: A storm outage would not be a manual switch on a single circuit, and the main hall stayed lit.

between: Owen Pryce: "I never set foot upstairs; I was in the basement from 8:30 to 9:40."
Kitchen porter: saw Owen coming from the Harbour Room corridor at about 9:25, clutching his tool bag.
keyContradictions.explanation: Owen cannot have been in the basement the whole time if he was seen coming from the Harbour Room side during the window.

between: Owen Pryce: "Nobody touches my key board, the keys never leave it."
The spare key tag HR-2 from his key board was found snapped off beside the opened case.
keyContradictions.explanation: The case was opened with a key, and the only spare left his key board and ended up at the scene.

between: Delia Marsh: "The compass would never be sold; I haven't spoken to any auction house."
Message slip: Hale & Crane Auctions confirmed her valuation of the compass for Monday.
keyContradictions.explanation: She did arrange an auction valuation. She is hiding the planned sale, not the theft.

between: Imogen Vale: "I never left the dining table all evening."
Her engraved lens cap was found on the bench beside the case.
keyContradictions.explanation: She was in the Harbour Room, but at 8:50, before Delia's 9:00 round confirmed the compass was still there.

scene.prompt: The Harbour Room of a small maritime museum at night during a storm: rain streaking tall arched windows, wood-panelled walls hung with ship paintings, a ship model on a shelf, a velvet rope. In the centre, an empty glass display case on a wooden pedestal with its small brass door ajar. A brass key tag lies on the parquet floor near the pedestal. A black camera lens cap rests on a polished wooden bench beside the case. A folded paper note sits on a small antique side table by the door, under a brass lamp. Dim amber light.
